name: Luric Road: Caelrun to Tagmira
terrain: Lake lowlands, then upland ridges. Bramblewood to the north. 18 miles, one day.
frequency: Roll once in the morning and once in the afternoon.
description: Roll d12 for the kind of encounter, then roll on that table.

table.encounter: Locals
Sent by someone
Common travellers
Factions
From Velgroth-Lucernia
From Imazuran
Hostile
The road itself
The caravan of **Taziri n'Khaleb**, bound for Tagmira's Wheel-Ring. Aelis Varrow will have the stew on.
**Penna** of the Hallan household walking east with letters and a basket for the Hallans in Tagmira.
**Caturo Hesk** leading 4 ponies west to sell in Caelrun. Will sell one to the party, on the spot.
**Rebur Tancin** with a cart of hides for Caelrun's oil pits; he'll come back with fish oil.
**Ordun Tarnes** with 3 carts of barley for Tagmira, where food is short this winter. He wants a fair price.
**Rondasek Elaran** walking west to see the lake, looking for a fight worth telling.
**Hildreth** walking east to the Gravefield of Thulda; the Tagmira widows asked for her.
**Merra** pacing the Tarnes barley fields along the road, counting the losses to birds.
A teamster sent west by **Aelis Varrow**: is Taziri's caravan late? She counts every rider.
A militiaman from **Hadran Throsk** to **Kelvan Bresul**: if the orcs come back to the northwest, will Caelrun send men?
**Gorran Fesk** pays 5gp to anyone who brings back his brother Aedd, who walked into the Bramblewood dead.
A Hallan boy with a crate of smoked fish from **Brecht Hallan** for his kin in Tagmira, and a carved toy for Pima.
**Medam**, sent by **Enni** the Ash-Wife to buy leeches from **Kessa**. He walks the whole way without a sound.
A boy sent by **Ambata Corr** with 2gp and a jug for Caelrun fish oil. Every north window lit this winter.
To be built: Bronze Host orcs.
To be built: the dead out of the Bramblewood.
To be built: bandits.
To be built: wolves on the ridges.
The lake drops behind. The road climbs onto goat paths and ridges.
Livestock bells on the ridges. A shepherd waves the party off his grazing.
The Bramblewood, a dark line to the north all afternoon.
Wool and iron charms tied to a roadside post, facing north.
A cart in the ditch. The ox went lame and was butchered where it fell.
Wind off the northern ridges, cold even in summer.
Juniper smoke from the Carnaxe curing lofts on the western ridge.
Nothing. Goats.
